originalAlarm.description: Memory dynamically allocated by `malloc`, indirectly via call to `extcon_class_init()` on line 107 is not freed after the last access at line 112, column 1.

presenceCondition: (and (= CONFIG_ANDROID true) (= CONFIG_SYSFS false) (= CONFIG_EXTCON true))
model:
(define-fun CONFIG_SYSFS () Bool
  false)
(define-fun CONFIG_ANDROID () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_EXTCON () Bool
  true)
reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (NEW, OVER-CONSTRAINED): 0dc77b6dabe.c (Linux extcon). Lines 1-3: '#ifdef CONFIG_ANDROID #define CONFIG_SYSFS #endif' — CONFIG_ANDROID=true always implies CONFIG_SYSFS=true. The presence condition requires SYSFS=false with ANDROID=true, which is an impossible/contradictory configuration. The underlying memory leak is real: switch_class is allocated via class_compat_register() (inside #ifdef CONFIG_SYSFS) in extcon_class_init()/create_extcon_class(), but extcon_class_exit() never frees it. This is a NEW bug (not in the vbdb known bug list, which lists DoubleOpOnResource for this file). OVER-CONSTRAINED because EXTCON=true is required, but the memory leak actually requires only SYSFS=true (implied by ANDROID=true); EXTCON controls module registration not the leak itself. The impossible SYSFS=false makes the stated presence condition unreachable.
